items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: this sweet looking Swiss girl asked me for an autograph... I asked her if she could have coffee with me the next day at 2 PM, and she accepted. She came the day after and we got along very well

ctx.x: On Christmas and New Year's day, Felix invited us to his country house in a place called Lugnorre which was about 50 miles from Bern to spend Christmas day. This was just a party for me and my musicians along with a few friends of Felix and his wife Liza, but only Norman Lester, "Bass" Hill and myself were there. We had taken some juice with us and Felix had plenty of white wine which is a famous party drink in Switzerland and we really bent elbows that day and night.

My engagement at the Chikito was to finish at the end of February 1950 and we were now within a few days from closing. The night of the 23rd a sweet looking Swiss girl was sitting in the balcony of the place. The Chikito was built in a circular form with a balcony that went around the place and the dance floor was down a floor below with tables around. There were tables in the balcony also and as I came by one of the tables going down stairs toget on the band-stand, this sweet looking Swiss girl asked me for an…

She came the day after and we got along very well between the little French that I spoke and making signs with out hands. She told me that her name was Lily, that she was Swiss and that she was a jazz fan although she didn't know too much about jazz musicians at the time. She had come a few times to the Chikito and was crazy about the band.
